string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and the country\'s political, cultural and international exchange center. With over 3,000 years of history, it is one of the Four Great Ancient Capitals of China. The city is renowned for its imperial palaces, gardens, parks, temples, gates and walls, including the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace and the Great Wall. Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and will host the 2022 Winter Olympics, making it the first city to host both events.

Shanghai is one of the four direct-administered municipalities of the People\'s Republic of China and is a global center for finance, innovation, shipping and technology. Located on the southern estuary of the Yangtze River, Shanghai is the most populous urban area in China, with a population of over 24 million. It is a popular tourist destination renowned for its historical landmarks such as the Bund, Yu Garden and the City God Temple, as well as the modern Lujiazui skyline featuring the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower. The Port of Shanghai is the world\'s busiest container port.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwest China and is the country\'s largest and most populous city by administrative area, with over 32 million residents. It is known as one of the "Four Furnaces" of China due to its extremely hot and humid summers. Chongqing is famous for its unique mountainous terrain, giving it the nickname "Mountain City" (Shancheng), and for its hot pot cuisine. The city is a major industrial hub and inland river port, located at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers. It served as the wartime capital of China during the Second Sino-Japanese War.

Tianjin is a metropolis and one of the four direct-administered municipalities of the People\'s Republic of China, with a population of over 15 million. Located on the shore of the Bohai Bay, it is the largest coastal city in Northern China and a major port and industrial center. Tianjoin has a rich history as a treaty port, with a blend of Chinese and European architectural influences visible in the Five Great Avenues area. The city is home to the Tianjin Binhai New Area, a national development zone, and hosts the annual Summer Davos Forum. Its cuisine is known for its goubuli steamed buns and mahua fried dough twists.
